sourcedFrom: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The RXD910Ti is a Nielsen-device can: it ships with a PB501 Mojave Booster Assembly and a PB440 1/2-28 Mojave piston, and the booster COMES APART for cleaning — housing, spring retainer, spring, piston and an o-ring. ⛔ Only Dead Air Mojave series pistons go in it. The front cap is aluminium, which is the one part that must never see an ultrasonic tank.

steps.title: Host clear before the can comes off
steps.action: Magazine out, action open, chamber checked. Dead Air refers you to your own firearm's manual for the clearing procedure itself.
steps.prose: This one lives on pistols and pistol-calibre carbines — the hosts most likely to be handled loaded.
steps.quote: CHECK YOUR FIREARM’S CHAMBER AND MAKE CERTAIN THAT THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND THE MAGAZINE REMOVED BEFORE PROCEEDING ANY FURTHER. IF THERE IS ANY QUESTION OR DOUBT, CONSULT THE OWNER’S MANUAL APPLICABLE TO YOUR FIREARM AS TO THE PROPER PROCEDURE FOR CLEARING AND/OR UNLOADING YOUR FIREARM.
steps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — General Considerations, p.5
steps.warn: THE SUPPRESSOR MAY BECOME EXTREMELY HOT AFTER USE. NEVER GRAB A HOT SUPPRESSOR AS IT CAN RESULT IN BURNS AND INJURY.

steps.title: Rated list, and the ceiling is .300 BLK / 10mm Auto / 400 Legend
steps.action: Confirm what it has been fed. Dead Air rates the RXD910Ti for 5.7x28, 9x19mm, .38 Special, .357 Mag, 10mm Auto, .300 Blackout and 400 Legend, and puts the pressure ceiling at .300 Blackout, 10mm Auto or 400 Legend.
steps.prose: A seven-cartridge list is unusual. Read it as a list, not as "pistol calibres".
steps.caution: Semi-auto 5.7x28 is rated but flagged: some platform and ammunition combinations perform poorly or damage the can.
steps.quote: THE RXD910TI IS RATED FOR 5.7X28, 9X19MM, .38 SPECIAL, .357 MAG, 10MM AUTO, .300 BLACKOUT, AND 400 LEGEND.
steps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Installation Notes, p.6

steps.title: Can off the barrel by the piston housing
steps.action: Grip the suppressor at the REAR, near the piston housing, and rotate the whole suppressor left-hand until it unthreads. Put the barrel's thread protector back on straight away so the threads do not get knocked about while the can is on the bench.
steps.prose: Gripping it at the front and twisting is what unscrews the front cap instead of the can.
steps.quote: To remove the suppressor, grip the suppressor in the rear near the piston housing and rotate the entire suppressor with a left-hand motion (as shown below) until the suppressor is completely unthreaded.
steps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Suppressor Installation and Removal — Removal, p.6

steps.title: Booster housing off — counter-clockwise, TL tool on the square features
steps.action: Rotate the booster housing counter-clockwise off the suppressor body until it separates. If it will not shift, put the SMALL end of the supplied TL tool on the square features of the housing, hold the suppressor firmly — a strap wrench if needed — and keep turning.
steps.prose: The housing is carbon-welded after a few hundred rounds. The tool exists because hands are not enough.
steps.quote: To begin disassembling the booster, rotate the booster housing counterclockwise from the suppressor body until the entire housing is separated from the main body.
steps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Booster Disassembly and Reassembly, p.8

steps.title: ⚠ The spring retainer is under tension — keep a hand on it
steps.action: Rotate the spring retainer counter-clockwise out of the piston housing, keeping constant pressure on it: it is under slight spring tension. Once it is off, the piston and spring pull straight out for cleaning, inspection or replacement.
steps.prose: "Slight" tension still launches a small steel part across a garage. Do it over a tray.
steps.caution: Work over a tray or a towel. The o-ring in the retainer is easy to lose.
steps.quote: Next, rotate the spring retainer in a counterclockwise motion until it is removed from the piston housing. Please note that the spring retainer is under slight spring tension, so maintain constant pressure on it during removal.
steps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Booster Disassembly and Reassembly, p.8

steps.title: Piston, housing, cap and control surfaces — and oil between spring and piston
steps.action: Get threads, tapers and mating surfaces free of debris, brushing lightly with nylon or brass and cleaning oil where there is build-up. Make sure the spring and piston are both clean of heavy build-up, then put a LIGHT coat of oil BETWEEN the spring and the piston. Wipe the excess off.
steps.prose: That oil film is what lets the booster actually stroke. A dry, carboned piston is the usual cause of a pistol that stops cycling suppressed.
steps.quote: Ensure the spring and piston are both clean and free of any large build-up. Apply a light coating of oil between the spring and the piston.
steps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Suppressor Cleaning and Maintenance, Step Two, p.9

steps.title: ⛔ The front cap is ALUMINIUM — keep it out of the ultrasonic tank
steps.action: Clean the internal body with non-toxic, water-soluble, biodegradable solutions. An ultrasonic tank WITHOUT heat and WITHOUT corrosive chemicals is fine for titanium, steel or Haynes 282 — but the RXD910Ti front cap is aluminium and Dead Air names it specifically as the part that must never go in.
steps.prose: This is the only Dead Air book in this batch that names the offending part rather than the material. Take it literally.
steps.quote: To enhance cleaning of the internal surfaces and geometry, an ultrasonic tank WITHOUT HEAT AND/OR CORROSIVE CHEMICALS may be used on any materials such as titanium, steel, or Haynes® 282®.
steps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Suppressor Cleaning and Maintenance, Step Three, p.9
steps.warn: NEVER USE ULTRA-SONIC TANKS FOR ALUMINUM PARTS SUCH AS THE RXD910Ti FRONT CAP.

steps.title: Booster back together — o-ring first, then piston, spring, retainer
steps.action: Check the o-ring is properly installed in the spring retainer FIRST. Insert the piston into the piston housing, slide the spring over the piston, position the retainer over the piston and — with slight downward pressure — rotate it onto the housing until it is fully seated. Then reinstall the assembled piston housing into the suppressor body and snug it with the TL tool.
steps.prose: The o-ring is the part that gets forgotten, and it is the first thing in the sequence for exactly that reason.
steps.quote: When reassembling, first ensure that the o-ring is properly installed in the spring retainer.
steps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Booster Disassembly and Reassembly — Reassembling the Booster, p.8

steps.title: Snug, no gaps, no rattle
steps.action: All components should fit snugly with no gaps or rattling. If something is not fully tightened, check the threads for damage or debris, clean both mating parts and repeat.
steps.prose: A booster that rattles is a booster that is not seated, and on a tilting-barrel pistol that shows up as a failure to cycle.
steps.quote: All components should fit snuggly with no gaps or rattling. If any component is not fully tightened, check threads for damage or debris. Clean both mating parts as necessary and repeat the tightening step.
steps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Inspection Upon Assembly, p.9

deepSteps.title: Front cap off — supplied tool or 11/16 inch, right-hand thread
deepSteps.action: The 9mm–10mm front cap is fitted at 35 inch-pounds at the factory and does not need removing in normal use. For cleaning it comes off counter-clockwise with the supplied tool or an 11/16 inch socket or wrench.
deepSteps.prose: Right-hand thread here — unlike the RXD22Ti's Front Cap Ring, which is the opposite. Do not carry one habit to the other can.
deepSteps.quote: The RXD910Ti comes with the 9mm-10mm front cap pre-installed at 35 inch-pounds. During normal use, it is not required to be removed. In the event of cleaning, the front cap can be removed by using the supplied tool or by using an 11/16” socket or wrench.
deepSteps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Front Cap Installation and Removal, p.7

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Mojave pistons only — and a fixed barrel needs the PB139 spacer
deepSteps.action: The PB440 1/2-28 piston is preinstalled and is designed specifically for this can; Dead Air says to use only Dead Air Mojave series pistons in it. On a FIXED barrel the booster must not stroke: you need the PB139 Mojave Fixed Barrel Spacer, or one of the fixed mounts — Xeno, KeyMicro, 3-Lug, P-Series.
deepSteps.prose: Running a live booster behind a fixed barrel is the classic pistol-can mistake. The spacer is what stops it.
deepSteps.aside: If you intend to use the supplied PB440 Piston on a fixed barrel, you will need to purchase the PB139 Mojave Fixed Barrel Spacer.
deepSteps.quote: Use only Dead Air Mojave series pistons with your RXD910Ti.
deepSteps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Installation Notes, p.6

deepSteps.title: If it walks loose under heat, degrease and use a MEDIUM-strength locker
deepSteps.action: Where high heat cycles loosen the mount on the firearm, degrease the threads and use a high-temperature thread locker on the barrel threads — Dead Air names Vibra-Tite 123, a medium-strength one, because many high-strength lockers need heat to remove.
deepSteps.prose: The trap is buying the strongest locker on the shelf and then needing a torch to service your own can.
deepSteps.quote: Dead Air recommends using a medium-strength, high temperature thread locker like Vibra-Tite 123 for average operating conditions.
deepSteps.cite: RXD910Ti 9MM OPTIMIZED • 10MM CAPABLE TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev110625 — Installation Notes, p.6

cleaning.name: BOOSTER — PISTON, SPRING, RETAINER
tasks: Housing off counter-clockwise, TL tool small end on the square features
Spring retainer out under CONSTANT PRESSURE — it is spring-loaded
Piston and spring pulled, cleaned of heavy build-up
Light oil BETWEEN the spring and the piston
O-ring checked and seated in the retainer before reassembly

cleaning.name: CONTROL SURFACES
tasks: Threads, tapers and mating faces brushed lightly with nylon or brass and oil
Excess wiped off with a shop or paper towel

cleaning.name: MAIN BODY
tasks: Ultrasonic WITHOUT heat and WITHOUT corrosive chemicals
⛔ The aluminium front cap NEVER goes in the tank

cleaning.name: FRONT CAP
tasks: Off counter-clockwise, supplied tool or 11/16 inch — right-hand thread

reassembly: O-ring seated in the spring retainer FIRST.
Piston into the piston housing, spring over the piston, retainer over the spring.
Slight downward pressure, retainer rotated on until fully seated against the housing.
Assembled piston housing back into the suppressor body, snugged with the TL tool.
Front cap, if removed, back to 35 inch-pounds.
Onto the host: piston aligned with the barrel threads, right-hand, until the rear of the piston seats on the barrel shoulder.
Snug everywhere, no gaps, no rattle.
fncheck: ⛔ If the piston will not thread smoothly onto your firearm, STOP — that is Dead Air's own instruction and the number is 801-857-4232. Otherwise: confirm the can is seated against the shoulder, nothing rotates or wobbles, and the booster housing is snugged into the body. Check the cartridge against the rated list. Then re-check tightness periodically through the shooting session — Dead Air asks for that explicitly, and a strap wrench or a glove is the way to retighten a warm can.
